parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized manual argparse alignment, exact bencoder/list/bytes repr output, BigInt-level arithmetic, ESM .mjs files, no external dependencies, and executable-only black-box probing.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It delegated behavioral probing through one workflow but retained implementation ownership in the parent process, which wrote every delivered module and entry file.
parallel.implementation: It built Python-like helpers for chars, bytes, int parsing, repr, print, bencode encode/decode, CLI formatting/parsing, and test14.mjs; after differential testing found a whitespace/int mismatch it patched the parser.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent wrote a coherent /output tree and artifact validation copied test14.mjs plus supporting lib modules with the expected entry present.
parallel.verification: The parent ran smoke tests and a differential harness; a later rerun was killed with exit 137, but official evaluation completed and passed 161/161 cases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow aggregate was killed and final.txt is empty because the agent process timed out, but no delivered implementation defect is shown by the official evaluation.

serial.requirements: The serial parent recognized the same migration constraints: ESM .mjs, manual argv parsing, bencoder behavior, Python integer semantics, exact output, and no npm dependencies.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It kept all work local in one process with workflows disabled, handling probing, module writing, patching, verification, and final reporting itself.
serial.implementation: It produced a smaller module tree covering bytes, pyint, bencode encoder/decoder, Python repr, argparse, arg type adapters, and test14.mjs, then fixed Unicode digit and negative-number matching gaps.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run assembled the /output directory once, audited imports and forbidden constructs, and artifact validation copied the expected entry and libraries successfully.
serial.verification: It verified documented samples, a 51/51 differential harness, 300 random integer pairs, 68 precision-boundary cases, and a constraint audit before closing.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished required work is visible; the final response notes a possible program-name divergence, but the official evaluator still passed the solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the Python program, required --a/--b argparse behavior, bencoder output, BigInt precision, ESM .mjs modules, no external dependencies, and executable-only probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same requirements, including manual argv parsing, no npm modules, hierarchical .mjs output, bencode behavior, and byte-for-byte print formatting.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference remained; both explored edge cases beyond the sample tests and passed the official suite.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split reference probing into a workflow, but the parent kept ownership of writing all deliverable modules and the entry point.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no delegation and performed probing, implementation, cleanup, and validation in one main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel run had probe-only child ownership while serial centralized the whole task; neither left implementation, integration, assembly, or pipeline ownership absent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Workflow child briefs gave each probe an executable path, source sketch, output schema, and a specific behavioral dimension; returned structured probe results were auxiliary.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial maintained task knowledge in the parent process and incorporated discovered facts directly into the local implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child handoff surfaces, but they were probe reports rather than separate interoperating code components, and no missing or stale interface affected the final artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent wrote a larger modular implementation under /output, including Python-like char, bytes, int, repr, print, bencode, CLI, and entry modules, then patched whitespace handling after a diff mismatch.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a smaller modular implementation under /output, then patched Unicode digit parsing and argparse negative-number matching after differential testing found a gap.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Implementation styles differed in module layout and discovered bug order, but both converged on the same required behavior before official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The background workflow produced some structured probe results but ended killed with the aggregate result null; parent progress did not depend on retrieving a final workflow return.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; all findings were immediately available in the main trajectory and the run ended with a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had unfinished probe lifecycle state while serial did not, but the unfinished workflow was not a required implementation or verifier return needed for the delivered solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent wrote and edited the submitted /output files; probe children used temporary/reference probing and did not write competing implementation files into the final tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote its /output tree from one trajectory and later audited the produced files and imports.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concrete shared-state collision or overwrite appears in the parallel run; both artifacts copied successfully with the expected entry point.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran smoke and differential tests, identified a real parsing mismatch, fixed it, and the official evaluator later passed all cases despite a later killed local diff rerun.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran documented samples, differential cases, randomized fuzzing, precision sweeps, and a final compliance audit before normal completion.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had cleaner closure and more explicit final reporting, while parallel had interrupted local verification late; official acceptance was identical at 161/161.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full agent budget and exited 143 after the workflow was killed, leaving final.txt empty but with a valid copied artifact and official pass.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 1242.25 seconds with provider reason agent_completed and more than 1100 seconds remaining.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure was noisier and timed out; serial closed normally. The timeout did not change the official task outcome or make the submitted artifact unverifiable.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant. The parallel run timed out after launching a probe workflow and leaving the workflow killed, but the parent-owned artifact was complete enough for the official evaluator. The serial run completed normally without delegation. Both current status.json evaluation records report solution_passed true with 161 of 161 samples passed, so no parallel coordination event explains a score difference.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used a broader module layout and background probe workflow; serial used a smaller single-process module layout and explicit final report. These differences did not change official correctness.
